paper.title_en: Phase-space topology of mass-varying dark matter and quintessence in Lyra geometry: a five-dimensional dynamical systems approach
paper.abstract_en: We investigate the cosmological dynamics of an interacting dark sector, comprising pressureless dark matter and an inverse power-law (IPL) quintessence field, formulated within the modified framework of Lyra geometry. To resolve the dimensional inconsistencies and isolated exchange channels prevalent in the literature, we introduce a dimensionally homogeneous, amalgamated coupling that phenomenologically governs the dark-sector energy transfer. By rigorously treating the IPL slope $\lambda = n/\phi$ as a fully dynamical variable rather than an artificially frozen parameter, we cast the modified Friedmann equations into a mathematically complete five-dimensional autonomous system. We demonstrate that the physically viable phase space admits exactly two fundamental critical points, both corresponding to Lyra de Sitter boundary states ($w_{\textrm{eff}}=-1$). Linear stability evaluation yields an exact, degenerate eigenvalue spectrum of $\{-3, -3, -3, 0, 0\}$. To resolve this non-hyperbolicity, we perform a rigorous nonlinear expansion on the center manifold. This fully dynamic 5D integration mathematically proves that the quintessence field's potential and kinetic energies are forced into a nonlinear algebraic decay (scaling as $y \propto N^{-1/4}$), acting merely as a transient catalyst to trigger the depletion of the matter sector. Consequently, both analytical and numerical results confirm that the ultimate late-time cosmic acceleration is inherently geometrical in origin, driven entirely by the persistent topography of the Lyra displacement field rather than a static scalar field attractor.
